children: Iraq exported 70 million barrels of oil in August and is currently exporting more than 3 million barrels per day, Oil Minister Basim Mohammed said in an interview with state TV on Tuesday.

The minister also said transporting crude by road from southern oilfields to a Kirkuk storage facility is expected to increase exports through Turkey's Ceyhan port to more than 600,000 barrels per day.

Iraq launched a pilot operation this month to ‌transport crude oil by road from its southern oilfields to Kirkuk in an effort to boost supplies to the northern export system and potentially increase shipments through Ceyhan.
The initiative forms part of broader Iraqi efforts to ​increase flows through the northern export route after the U.S.-Israeli war ⁠with
disrupted Iraq's shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, its main export ​route.
Production from oilfields in Iraq's Kurdistan region currently stands at about 200,000 bpd, the minister added.
